title: 育儿与教育：批判性思维启蒙 — Day 36

questions.question: 孩子说：「小明就是个坏孩子。」按区分事实与观点的思路，家长最好怎么回应？
options: 认同他的感受，并提醒他以后离小明远一点，免得受到影响
告诉他每个人的看法都不一样，这种评价别人的事本来就没有对错之分
纠正他不能随便说别人坏，每个小朋友都有自己的优点
问他「坏孩子」是事实还是想法，小明具体做了什么让他这么觉得
questions.explanation: 幼儿倾向把所有陈述都当客观事实，父母用「这是事实还是你的想法」这类语言搭脚手架，孩子才学会给观点贴标签，并把笼统判断拆回具体事实。顺着认同是把观点当事实强化；而「什么都没有对错」走到了相对主义，事实是存在的。
questions.question_en: A child says, 'Xiao Ming is just a bad kid.' Following the idea of separating fact from opinion, how should a parent respond?
options_en: Validate the feeling and remind them to keep away from Xiao Ming so they aren't influenced
Tell them everyone sees things differently, so there's no right or wrong in matters like this
Correct them that they mustn't call others bad, since every child has their own good points
Ask whether 'bad kid' is a fact or their opinion, and what exactly Xiao Ming did that made them feel that way
questions.explanation_en: Young children tend to treat every statement as objective fact. When parents scaffold with language like 'Is that a fact or what you think?', children learn to label opinions and break sweeping judgments back down into specific facts. Agreeing reinforces opinion as fact; 'there's no right or wrong' slides into relativism, though facts do exist.

questions.question: 孩子兴奋地转述：「同学说吃了这种糖能变聪明！」按「校准信任」的思路，家长最好怎么回应？
options: 告诉他网上和同学说的话大多不可信，以后听到什么都要多留个心眼
直接告诉他这是瞎说，不要相信同学的话
让他去问老师，老师怎么说就以老师的意见为准
和他一起想：怎么才能知道是不是真的？谁说的、有证据吗？
questions.explanation: 校准信任是按证据和来源决定信几分，把「信不信」转成「怎么查」。直接说「瞎说」给了结论却没给方法；把一切讲成不可信会养出犬儒而非明辨；只服从权威则会信错。校准也包括该信时要信。
questions.question_en: A child excitedly reports, 'My classmate says eating this candy makes you smarter!' Following the idea of 'calibrated trust,' how should a parent respond?
options_en: Tell them most of what they hear online or from classmates can't be trusted, so stay wary
Tell them straight out it's nonsense and not to believe what classmates say
Have them ask the teacher, and take whatever the teacher says as the answer
Think it through together: how could we find out if it's true? Who said it, and is there evidence?
questions.explanation_en: Calibrated trust means deciding how much to believe based on evidence and source, turning 'believe it or not' into 'how do we check.' Saying 'nonsense' hands over a conclusion without a method; treating everything as untrustworthy breeds cynicism rather than discernment; deferring to authority alone leads to believing the wrong things. Calibration also means believing when belief is warranted.

questions.question: 看动画时插播玩具广告，5 岁的孩子喊「我要这个！」按早期媒介素养的思路，家长最好怎么做？
options: 指出这是广告，问他：做这个广告的公司最想让我们做什么？
马上换台或关掉，不让孩子接触到任何广告内容
跟他讲清楚这个玩具太贵、家里不买，然后赶紧转移他的注意力
告诉他广告里说的全是骗人的，以后都别相信
questions.explanation: 8 岁以下孩子难以区分广告与节目，也看不出说服意图，所以要给他装一个「谁做的、想让我干嘛」的提问滤镜。只堵不疏，孩子脱离监管后毫无抵抗力；把一切讲成骗人的，养出的是犬儒而不是明辨。
questions.question_en: A toy ad interrupts a cartoon and the 5-year-old shouts, 'I want that!' Following early media-literacy thinking, what should the parent do?
options_en: Point out that it's an ad and ask: what does the company that made it most want us to do?
Change the channel or turn it off right away so the child isn't exposed to any ads
Explain that the toy is too expensive and you won't buy it, then distract them
Tell them everything ads say is a lie and never to believe them
questions.explanation_en: Children under about 8 struggle to tell ads from programs and don't see the persuasive intent, so the goal is a habit of asking 'Who made this, and what do they want from me?' Blocking without teaching leaves kids defenseless once unsupervised; calling everything a lie breeds cynicism instead of discernment.
